Leadership capabilities for the next decade

Sustaining ethical, inclusive workplaces
Event Summary:
"Krish Shankar - Independent Director
Ex National President NHRDN

AI will shift learning from periodic training to continuous real-time development, where employees receive instant feedback and guidance while performing their tasks.
The workplace will evolve into an AI-supported ecosystem, where multiple digital assistants, copilots, and AI agents help employees make faster and better decisions.
AI will function as a virtual manager and advisor, providing employees with guidance, problem-solving support, and access to organizational knowledge.
Managers will rely on AI-driven insights to monitor team performance, enabling data-based leadership instead of manual supervision.
Enterprise AI agents will automate complex organizational processes, such as recruitment, by generating job descriptions, screening candidates, and conducting preliminary interviews.
The value created by individual employees will significantly increase, as AI augments human capabilities and improves productivity.
Future talent will be defined by the ability to synthesize information, recognize patterns, and imagine new possibilities, rather than perform routine tasks.
Frontline employees will become highly empowered, as AI tools enable them to make faster decisions with greater autonomy.
HR will play a central strategic role in the AI-driven organization, ensuring ethical AI usage, managing biases, and preparing employees for human-AI collaboration.
The real challenge for organizations is not building AI, but integrating multiple AI systems responsibly and effectively, while preserving the human element in work."
